kubernetes.label: Kubernetes
points: Pending pod: kubectl describe pod -> FailedScheduling event tells you CPU/mem/affinity/taint shortfall.
CrashLoopBackOff: kubectl logs --previous first, then check probes and resource limits (OOMKilled = exit 137).
HPA scales on requests, not limits; pick a metric that reflects load (concurrency for I/O-bound, not just CPU).
VPA and HPA should not both scale the same resource metric - VPA for right-sizing, HPA for horizontal scale.
Cluster autoscaler scales up on unschedulable pods, scales down on underutilized nodes (respects PDBs).
Readiness probe should check real dependency health, not just a TCP/port check - avoids zombie backends.
GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux) reverts manual kubectl edits - emergency fixes must go through Git, not live edits.

cicd.label: CI/CD & Jenkins
points: Jenkins + GitHub: GitHub Branch Source plugin + webhook to /github-webhook/, credentials via Jenkins Credentials store.
Branch exclusion: Branch Source behaviors (regex filter) in the multibranch job, or a when { branch } guard in Jenkinsfile.
Promotion pattern: build -> test -> containerize -> push to registry -> deploy to staging -> canary/blue-green to prod.
GitOps drift: controller reconciles live state back to Git - any out-of-band change gets silently reverted.
Trunk-based + PR review + required status checks is the default safe branch strategy to name.
Rollback should be a one-step operation (revert commit / repoint traffic), not a manual multi-step scramble.

agentic-ai.label: Agentic AI / LLMOps
points: LangChain = building blocks; LangGraph = explicit state machine + checkpointing for reliable multi-step agents.
CrewAI/AutoGen = multi-agent, role-based orchestration.
Tool calls: LLM returns structured function name + JSON args; orchestrator validates and executes, feeds result back.
Agent auth: workload identity / short-lived tokens for the agent itself; per-tool authorization scope for user actions.
Observability: trace every step (prompt, tool calls, tokens, latency, cost) - LangSmith/Langfuse/Phoenix or custom logging.
Deploy on K8s: HPA on concurrency (not CPU); external store (Redis/DB) for conversation/checkpoint state, never in-pod memory.

mlops.label: MLOps / Model Monitoring
points: Monitor both layers: infra (latency, errors, replicas) AND model (data drift, prediction drift, accuracy/F1).
Drift metrics: PSI / KL divergence / KS test on feature distributions vs. training baseline.
Model versioning: registry-based (Vertex AI Model Registry / MLflow), canary new versions, one-step rollback by version ID.
Drift detected -> alert -> runbook: sanity-check upstream schema, then retrain / rollback / accept as a defined decision path.
Retraining is a pipeline (Vertex AI Pipelines/Kubeflow/Composer), not a manual step - same eval gates as the original model.
Clean ownership line: data science owns model/training/eval; platform owns serving, CI/CD, scaling, and monitoring.

terraform.label: Terraform / IaC
points: State conflicts: terraform plan first (no changes), terraform state show/import to reconcile - never blind re-apply.
Prevent conflicts: remote state + native locking (GCS backend / Terraform Cloud), CI/CD-only applies, no local applies.
Validation blocks on variables + OPA/Sentinel policy-as-code in CI to hard-block risky changes before apply.
6 Rs for migration decisions: rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire, retain.

sre.label: SRE / Incident Response
points: Incident STAR: situation/impact -> diagnostic steps in order -> the fix -> RCA + concrete prevention.
Multi-window multi-burn-rate alerting: fast burn = page now, slow burn = ticket, tuned off SLO error budget.
Retry storms: exponential backoff + jitter, circuit breakers, short timeouts, load shedding/bulkheads.
Cost spikes: billing breakdown by service/day, cross-reference with deploy/Terraform change history first.
Noisy neighbor: PriorityClass + ResourceQuota + tainted/dedicated node pool beats one-cluster-per-team.

networking.label: GCP Networking
points: 404/502 debug path: DNS -> load balancer -> ingress controller -> service -> pod endpoints, in that order.
VPC Service Controls: prevents data exfiltration across project boundaries; adds operational friction - know both sides.
Cross-service latency regressions are usually shared-resource contention (node, DB, cache), not the new code path itself.
LB health check and Kubernetes readiness probe must check the same real signal, or you get zombie backends.

coding.label: Coding Patterns
points: Median of two sorted arrays: binary search the smaller array for a partition, O(log(min(m,n))).
Longest palindromic substring: expand-around-center from every index (odd + even), O(n^2).
Sliding window (longest substring without repeat): track last-seen index, jump window start past repeat.
Two Sum: single pass with a value->index hash map, O(n).
Cycle detection: Floyd's tortoise and hare, O(1) space.
Topological sort / cycle detection in a dependency graph: Kahn's algorithm (indegree + queue).

behavioral.label: Behavioral / STAR
points: Tell me about yourself: 3 parts, under 90s - summary, relevant career thread, close tied to this role.
Always have 2-3 questions ready for the interviewer: technical depth, team process, growth/first-90-days.
Frame contributions around ownership + measurable impact, not just tool names.
When experience is thin on a topic, say so honestly and pivot to the adjacent thing you do own.
